drafts.walkScript: People admire Mr Darcy at first, "till his manners gave a disgust" on line 31. That means the way he acted put people off him. Lines 32 and 33 say he was "proud" and "above his company". He acted as if he were better than everyone there. Being angry that the ball closed early is Mr Bingley, at line 37.

Lines 7 and 8 say "Named things went in the first box to be returned." Lines 8 and 9 say the unnamed box went to "the charity collection on Friday morning". At lines 13 and 14 he keeps the rule, even for a girl who has left. Lines 31 and 32 show he knows the jumper is his. Line 33 puts his jumper in "the Friday box", so the rule bends for him alone.

On line 37 Reuben only "passed the noticeboard" on his way to a bin bag. Line 38 says the sheet is for "September football trials". On line 47 he explains letting his named jumper go: "It won't fit me next year." September trials belong to next year too, and he is already giving up on next year. So the room at the bottom is a space he is not going to fill.

Lines 7 and 8 say named things went in the first box "to be returned". Lines 8 and 9 say the other box was going to "the charity collection". At line 13 the cardigan's owner "had left in Year Four". Line 14 says he put it in the returns box "anyway". He knew she had gone, yet chose returning over giving it to charity.
Turn to lines 18 and 19, after his long time in the cellar underground. The carol hits his "dulled hearing". So his ears have changed, not the birds. The rabbits come later.
Line 14 says "she began to fear". Lines 14 and 15 say he might be "flying about from one place to another". So she fears he will never settle. The dinner comes earlier, the guests later.
